newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX idle in early dealings with weaker dlr.
newsitem.headline: German DAX idle in early dealings with weaker dlr.

text.p: German shares were on Wednesday unable to build further on the late gains made in post-bourse trade with a stronger Wall Street on Tuesday as dealers said the weaker dollar held dealings back.

The DAX-30 index of leading German shares rose 36.13 points, 1.09 percent, to 3,363.81 in early dealings to catch up with Tuesday's post-bourse rally. The IBIS index of all-day electronic trade eased 4.38 points to 3,364.88 by 0915 GMT.
June DAX futures were a point higher at 3,374.0, with the the dollar traded below the 1.730 mark level at 1.725 marks in early European dealings.
With turnover low and even 1996 result details from industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, failing to excite the market, dealers saw a narrow day-range.
One said the DAX index was unlikely to trade much outside the 3,340-90 range throughout the day.

Dealers said new result details released from Daimler-Benz were being viewed positively but not with the same enthusiasm that greeted recent figures from BMW. Upgrades were nonetheless expected to result from an analyst meeting later today.

Daimler's shares were traded five pfennigs higher in IBIS trade to 139.35 just before bourse open after earlier reaching an all-time high of 142.40. Turnover, at 710,000 shares dealt, was the highest of the day so far but not seen as exceptional.
When the bourse opened, Daimler shares were up 1.40 marks to 138.30 marks.
Dealers said a move by the group to issue 1.1 billion marks in mandatory convertible notes to strengthen its capital base was not being seen positively.
Drugs group Schwarz Pharma, which late Tuesday said group net profits rose 14.4 percent in 1996 and further a profit growth was expected in 1997, rose 3.50 marks to 137.0.
